thesis: Oklo builds compact 15-75 MW factory-built Aurora Powerhouse fast reactors on a 'build, own, operate' model with long-term PPAs, targeting AI data centers and industrial off-takers. A DOE startup authorization for its Groves Isotope Test Reactor clears the way for fuel loading and first criticality, a major near-term de-risking milestone, while a Meta 1.2 GW Ohio campus partnership and a Trump-administration-backed ~$200M advanced-nuclear initiative (with Microsoft, Nvidia and X-energy) validate demand. Pre-revenue with over $1B cash and essentially no debt, but the stock has round-tripped from a ~$194 high to near its 52-week low, and HALEU fuel supply plus NRC licensing remain key risks ahead of first commercial operation targeted for late 2027/2028.

drivers: Groves Isotope Test Reactor reaches first criticality on schedule, proving the fuel and licensing pathway
Aurora-INL progresses through NRC licensing without major delays
Meta Ohio 1.2 GW campus proceeds and additional LOIs convert to binding PPAs
Trump-administration ~$200M advanced-nuclear-for-AI initiative accelerates deployment and policy tailwinds
First commercial operation confirmed for late 2027/2028, re-rating the stock toward its prior highs

risks: NRC licensing delays push first commercial operation into 2029-2030
HALEU fuel supply constraints limit deployment speed
First-of-a-kind commissioning issues emerge at Groves or Aurora-INL
Continued nuclear-sector profit-taking and high beta drive further downside
LOI pipeline fails to convert to binding, financeable PPAs

base_case.assumptions: Groves reaches criticality and Aurora-INL advances through NRC licensing with modest slippage; Meta Ohio Phase 1 and initial PPA conversions proceed; over $1B cash funds the plan without near-term dilution; stock trades on execution milestones between its 52-week low and prior highs. Consensus avg target ~$84 implies roughly 2x upside from current levels.

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — cash burn, runway, and milestone updates
Groves Isotope Test Reactor fuel loading and first criticality following DOE startup authorization — major near-term de-risking milestone
Aurora-INL progress and NRC licensing advancement
LOI-to-PPA conversions and Meta 1.2 GW Ohio campus timeline
First commercial operation — major derisking event

key_risks: NRC licensing risk — no non-water-cooled commercial reactor has yet been licensed; delays push out first revenue
HALEU fuel supply scarcity constrains deployment (Russia banned as supplier)
First-of-a-kind technology execution risk at Groves and Aurora-INL commercial scale
Extreme valuation and sentiment volatility — stock round-tripped from ~$194 to near its 52-week low on nuclear-sector profit-taking (beta 1.16)
Pre-revenue; first commercial operation is ~2 years out, testing investor patience
